requirement.summary: KDS2-DEV-03-2-20: Get tickets which within last 24 hours
requirement.description:
Goal

Change GET /api/kds/v1/getTickets so it returns all non-delivered, non-void (active/working) tickets plus delivered and void tickets modified within the last 24 hours, replacing the current fixed “last 50” count limit. Add pagination so clients can fetch large result sets in pages.

Success criteria

- Active/working tickets (statuses other than delivered and void/cancelled) are returned in full — not limited by the 24-hour window or pagination count cap.

- Delivered tickets are included only if ticket.modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Void/cancelled tickets are included only if ticket.modified >= now - 24 hours.

- The fixed limits DELIVERED_TICKET_RETRIEVE_LIMIT (50) and VOID_TICKET_RETRIEVE_LIMIT (50) are removed or replaced by the time filter.

- API accepts pagination params (e.g. page, pageSize) and returns page metadata (e.g. total count, current page, page size).

- Existing clients without pagination params get sensible defaults (e.g. page 0, default page size).

- OpenAPI docs updated to describe the combined result set, time filter, and pagination behavior.

Implementation notes

- Result set composition: Merge three groups:

- All active/working tickets for the display (unchanged behavior).

- Delivered tickets where modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Void/cancelled tickets where modified >= now - 24 hours.

- Primary touchpoints: TicketApiControllerV1, TicketApiServiceImpl, TicketServiceImpl, and TicketEntryRepository queries (findLastXDeliveredTicketIds, findLastXFullyVoidedTicketIds, etc.).

- Time filter: Use Ticket.modified >= Instant.now().minus(24, HOURS) for delivered and void tickets only.

(Note: “modified <= current - 24 hours” would mean older than 24h; for “last 24 hours” the condition should be >=.)

- Replace count-based queries in getTicketEntriesFromLastXDeliveredTicket / getTicketEntriesFromLastXVoidTicket with time-filtered queries; add/use a DB index on (shop_id, modified) if needed for performance.

- Pagination scope: Apply pagination to the combined response (active + recent delivered + recent void), or paginate only delivered/void while always returning all active tickets. Page size is set to 500 by default.

- Response shape: Extend TicketsMessage or wrap it with pagination fields (page, pageSize, totalElements, totalPages).

requirement.release_notes:
# Enhancements: [Jira-68370] POS Launcher / POS Client (Windows) - Issues of POS WSPS feature

## Descriptions

Improves reliability and clarity of **Workstation Printing Service (WSPS)** for outlets using embedded print on POS workstations.

### Panel status

- Status is clearer while a station takes up the print role:
  - **Starting** — role assigned; printing has not started yet  
    *(was: often looked like Standby right after Start)*
  - **Running** — print traffic is active
  - **Standby** — no activity for about **90 seconds**  
    *(was: Standby did not always appear when the holder went silent)*
- Status refreshes while the panel stays open  
  *(was: health could look stale until the panel was reopened)*

### Panel actions

- **Start**
  - Select any eligible online station, then start WSPS on that station  
    *(was: Start mainly acted on the current workstation)*
- **Pause / Restore**
  - Still only on **this** workstation

### Who can hold the WSPS role

- Eligibility follows the **Enable Embed Printing Core Service** setting only  
  *(was: also required a Windows client)*
- Stations with the setting **Disable** are not nominated

### Launcher behaviour

- WSPS runs only when the launcher has a valid WSPS port configured
- If that port cannot be opened:
  - POS login and normal launcher service continue
  - WSPS stays off for that session  
    *(was: a WSPS port failure could block the whole launcher)*

## Setup

- Deploy the updated **POS launcher** and **POS Client (Windows)** together  
  *(altered: both sides must match so the embed-print Enable / Disable setting is recognized correctly)*

requirement.summary: IP2COM - Recover USB printing after printer power-off; cleaner service stop; optional auto-restart for long disconnect
requirement.description:
Background

When a USB kitchen printer is powered off while idle, printing may stay unavailable after power-on until the IP2COM service is restarted manually. This change improves automatic recovery and makes service stop release resources cleanly.

What it does

- After USB printer power-off / power-on, reconnects more reliably and can resume printing without a manual service restart

- Speeds reconnect when the USB device is plugged in or powered on again

- Uses shorter reconnect waits at first, then longer waits if the device stays offline (USB only; other device types keep existing behaviour)

- Optional DisconnectWatchdog (off by default): if reconnect keeps failing for a long time, can restart the IP2COM service, with longer waits between restarts overnight so the service is not restarted every few minutes

- Service stop / force-stop closes printers, network connections, and related work properly before exit

- Clearer logs for expected disconnects; less noise when debug is off

- Small HTML printer spacing fix (  handling)

Setup

- New option: disconnect_watchdog under [setup] — leave 0 unless the site needs auto service restart on long disconnect
requirement.release_notes:
Enhancements: [HERO-68252] Recover USB printing after printer power-off; cleaner service stop; optional auto-restart for long disconnect
Descriptions:
IP2COM improves how it handles USB printers that disconnect and come back.
Service stop and restart now release printer and network connections more cleanly.
An optional Disconnect Watchdog can restart the IP2COM service automatically if a device stays disconnected for a long time. It is off by default.
When enabled, early retries are more frequent; if the device stays offline longer, later restarts become much less frequent, so the PC is not disrupted every few minutes.
Still disconnected after an automatic service restart, later restarts wait longer each time (about 5 minutes for the first six, then 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, and up to 8 hours).
Features:
USB reconnect reliability improvements
USB printers may disconnect or be power-cycled during normal operation.
Due to OS limitations, automatic reconnecting was not always reliable and sometimes required an IP2COM service restart.
This update improves automatic reconnect handling and adds optional recovery for extended disconnects.
Expected behavior
Short USB disconnects
Printer reconnects automatically.
Printing resumes without manual IP2COM restart.
Long USB disconnects
Watchdog disabled: continues retrying reconnect indefinitely.
Watchdog enabled: perform controlled service restarts with progressively longer retry intervals.
Notes for implementation / support:
Applies to USB printers used with IP2COM.
Other printer device types keep their previous reconnect handling and timing.
Setup:
In config.ini, under [setup], add restart_service_on_long_disconnect for on / off the feature
Default: restart_service_on_long_disconnect=0, which keeps Disconnect Watchdog off.
Set restart_service_on_long_disconnect=1 only if the site needs automatic IP2COM service restart after a long reconnect failure.
Existing option restart_service_on_init_error is unchanged and remains separate from Disconnect Watchdog.
Recommendation: keep restart_service_on_long_disconnect=0 for most sites. Turn it on only if a long disconnect still needs a service restart and the site accepts occasional automatic restarts of IP2COM, affecting all devices on that service.

requirement.summary: Simple Smart Station - Fail to leave standalone mode if unable to connect to master server upon launcher starts
requirement.description:
It is related to Simple Smart Station model.

When starting the smart station launcher, if smart station cannot connect to master server, it is unable to leave standalone mode if the connection to master server is recovered.

Workflow

1. Smart station under standalone mode

2. Restart the launcher service while it is unable to connect to the master server

3. Login to the smart station

4. Click “leave standalone mode” while it is able to connect to the master server

5. Dialog box shown “Fail to connect to server master”

Expected Result:

Leave standalone mode pass if the connection to master server is recovered.

requirement.summary: Android POS App - Apply Goggle Play policy for camera permission, feature declaration, and compliance
requirement.description:
Description

The Android POS application currently has unmanaged camera permission declarations and implementation gaps that risk runtime crashes (SecurityException), unintended Google Play installation restrictions on non-camera hardware, and compliance alignment regarding data safety.

Key Observations

- Implicit Feature Declaration: The app declares <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.CAMERA" /> in the AndroidManifest.xml without an explicit <uses-feature> tag, causing Google Play to implicitly set android:required="true".

- Runtime Permission Handling: Camera APIs may be invoked without robust runtime permission checks, risking a SecurityException on devices running Android 6.0 (API level 23) and higher.

- Data Safety Declaration:

- Collected Camera Frames: The Google Play Data Safety form must accurately reflect how camera frames/photos are handled (e.g., ephemeral local processing for barcode scanning without server upload).

- [Updated 02/09/2026] App Interactions: App interaction data is collected for app functionality.

Technical Impacts

- Installation Restrictions: Devices without a built-in camera are currently blocked from installing the POS app due to the implicit android:required="true" hardware feature requirement.

- App Stability / Crashes: Executing camera operations without checking and requesting runtime permissions leads to unhandled SecurityException crashes.

Follow-Up:

Explicitly Declare Camera Hardware Feature

- Define camera hardware is needed explicitly

Implement Runtime Permission Checks

- Ensure camera permission is validated before invoking any camera intent or hardware API.

- Implement standard permission request flows with graceful denial handling.

Google Play Data Safety & Disclosure Alignment

- [Updated 02/09/2026] App Interactions

- App interaction data is collected for app functionality and is therefore declared as 'Collected' under App Activity > App Interactions in the Play Console.

- Update the Google Play Console Data Safety form accordingly

- Camera Frames

- Confirm and document that camera frames are processed ephemerally on-device (live barcode scanning) and are not persistently stored or transmitted to external servers.

- Update the Google Play Console Data Safety form accordingly.

- [Updated 02/09/2026] The Google Play Console's 'Photos and videos' disclosure applies only to raw image or video file transmissions. Since our Android app processes camera frames locally on-device and only sends the parsed string value to the backend, no media files are collected. Leaving the 'Photos and videos' category undeclared is still remain safe.

-

- References: Understand app privacy & security practices with Google Play's Data safety section - Computer - Google Play Help

requirement.description:
Cloud Hosted Phase 3 - Highest Priority POS Function keys

The following POS functions are required to be fully supported in Offline Controller (Smartstation / SS) during Cloud-hosted (CH) downtime.

Park Order - core function for Digital Dine

Expectation:

Park Order records should be synced between Cloud Hosted and Offline Controller.

- When Cloud Hosted (CH) is unreachable, and after switching to SS + MQ activation. Then SS will start receiving new park order records from MQ.

- Upon CH recovery and operation switch back from SS to CH, park orders created in SS should be sync back to CH. CH should work as the primary and receiving new park orders from Digital Dine (POSgAPI).
